page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core running at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional memory performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top tier (top 10%) and large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching a strong 296.76 GB/sec. Database operations are also strong, scoring 24183.55 in Passmark testing. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the top 25% at 198.16 GB/sec. However, the server exhibits limitations in large language model workloads, with text generation for 70B models and prompt processing for 7B models scoring in the poor and weak categories, respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gd.4xlarge offers high resource density by combining dedicated ARM64 processing cores, a substantial memory footprint, and high-speed local NVMe storage without the overhead of external storage attachments. This profile makes the server highly suitable for memory-intensive and database workloads, such as caching layers, relational databases, data analytics, and high-throughput decompression tasks, while it is less optimal for heavy AI inference workloads.
